name: Liquid Ether
description: WebGL2 fluid simulation background that renders flowing colored liquid which reacts to pointer movement and clicks, with an idle auto-demo motion and an intro animation.
contents: Container div with a single full-size WebGL canvas
behavior: Runs a GPU fluid solver (advection, pressure projection) and colors the flow from a gradient palette
Pointer movement anywhere on the window pushes the fluid
Pointer press triggers a burst when clickBurst is on
Auto-demo moves a virtual cursor after the pointer has been idle for autoResumeDelay
Intro animation plays on first mount
Pauses when offscreen or the tab is hidden, recovers from WebGL context loss
Respects prefers-reduced-motion by skipping the intro and auto-demo loop
editableByProps: Fluid colors, intensity, background color and light mode
Pointer force, brush size, persistence, viscosity and edge bounce
Simulation resolution and max device pixel ratio for performance
Click burst, auto-demo speed, strength and resume delay, intro on or off
Container sizing and positioning through className and style

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the number of pressure solver iterations
needsCodeEdit.where: PRESSURE_STEPS constant at the top of the file

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the rendering pixel and grid cell limits
Change how colors are shaded from the flow
Listen to pointer only inside the component instead of the whole window
needsCodeEdit.where: window.addEventListener pointermove, pointerdown, pointerup calls in the main useEffect

fixed: Needs WebGL2 and float color buffer support, otherwise nothing renders and the canvas stays blank with no fallback
Container is h-full w-full, so the parent must have a defined height and should be positioned
Listens to pointer events on the whole window, not only over the component, so content above it should use pointer-events as needed
Canvas is aria-hidden and not interactive itself
Heavy GPU load on low-end mobile devices, lower resolution or maxDevicePixelRatio there
